name: DC gear motor (TT, 3–6 V)
description: Yellow TT gear motor used on 2WD robot cars: about 200 rpm at 6 V. Never wire it to an Arduino pin (it needs 150–1500 mA): drive it from an L298N output (OUT1/OUT2 or OUT3/OUT4). Swap A and B to reverse it.

pins.label: M+
pins.description: Motor terminal. The shaft turns forward (positive rpm) when A is more positive than B.

props.label: Rated voltage
props.description: Voltage the no-load speed and currents below are given at.

props.label: No-load speed
props.description: Output-shaft speed with no load at the rated voltage (after the gearbox). TT motors: 120–250 rpm depending on gear ratio.

props.label: Stall current
props.description: Current with the shaft blocked at the rated voltage. Sets the winding resistance (ratedVoltage / stallCurrent).

props.label: No-load current
props.description: Current when spinning freely at the rated voltage. Sets friction.

props.label: Spin-up time constant
props.description: Time to reach 63 % of the final speed after a voltage step (rotor + gearbox inertia).

footprint: TT gearbox motor, 70 × 22 × 18 mm, 5.4 mm double-flat shaft

bindings.description: Output-shaft speed in rpm, signed (positive = A more positive than B).
Output-shaft speed in rad/s, signed. Physics reads this to turn the wheel.

mechanical.source: TT gear motor (shaft out of both sides)

sourcing.generic: TT gear motor 3 to 6 V, 1:48, double shaft
